Subject: Hosted API commit onramp — initial numbers and latency constraints

Hi Soojin / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — LumenLabs is excited about the latency profile and the batching/caching approach you showed. We’re preparing to formalize an initial hosted commit and wanted to share rough volumes so you can advise on the right tier and any soft-throttle/guardrail recommendations.

Quick context: our core inference workload is chat autosuggest across mobile + web. Expected monthly token consumption for Q4 is ~1.2B tokens with peak bursts up to 180k tokens/min during promos. We anticipate a 3-month ramp (50% in month 1 -> 100% by month 3) if we lock a tier and SLA.

Questions:
- What commit bands would you recommend for predictable throughput and to stay within a 250–350ms 95th percentile latency target?
- Do you support a soft-throttle/circuit-breaker cadence to protect SLOs during bursts (we prefer graceful degradation vs. outright failures)?
- Can you share an SOW + indicative pricing for a 12-month term with a 3-month ramp?

Attached: traffic_curve.csv (sample hourly token curve).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

Best,
Anya
Head of Platform Integrations
LumenLabs

Subject: Re: Hosted API commit onramp — initial numbers and latency constraints

Hi Anya — really helpful data, thanks.

Short answer up front: yes, we can support a 3-month ramp into a committed band that meets your latency target with a soft-throttle fallback. Below is a recommended staging plan and the operational safeguards we propose.

Staged commit recommendation (provisional):
- Month 1 (onramp): 400M tokens committed (provisioned capacity, burst enabled)
- Month 2: 800M tokens committed
- Month 3+: 1.2B tokens monthly committed (steady state)

Why staged: this lets us monitor sequence lengths and actual arrival shape; our kernel selection and KV cache hit rate typically improve after the first multimillion-request window, lowering per-token latency and cost.

Soft-throttle / graceful degradation: we propose a multi-tier fallback policy:
1) Prefix/KV cache priming and adaptive batching to preserve 95p latency under normal bursts.
2) Canary fallbacks to a small-quant (higher throughput, slightly lower quality) model variant when 95p latency crosses target for >30s.
3) Controlled soft-throttle that returns 429-lite with optional degraded payload (summary-only responses) for non-critical routes — we’d coordinate which API routes are eligible.

SLA & monitoring: we’ll provide a per-route latency dashboard, token-level cost breakdowns, and an alert (and auto-fallback) policy. We’ll include a three-month ramp clause in the SOW.

Next steps:
- Ben: can you draft an indicative pricing SOW with the staged commit bands and DocuSign-ready SOW v2?
- Karthik: can you confirm legal/procurement items we need to surface (PO cadence, invoicing cadence) for a 12-month term?
- Anya: share any internal route priorities (which endpoints must be protected first) — we’ll map them to fallback scopes.

I’ve attached a short checklist (ops prep) to this thread and will follow up with a time to align.

— Soojin
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted API commit onramp — indicative pricing

Anya — thanks for the curve, this helps a lot.

Indicative headroom pricing (high-level, subject to SOW sign):
- Month 1 commit 400M: $28k/mo (effective unit pricing tier A)
- Month 2 commit 800M: $50k/mo (tier B blended pricing)
- Month 3 steady 1.2B: $68k/mo (tier C + small discount for annual term)

Notes:
- Pricing assumes prefix caching and standard batching. Extremely high burst minutes (180k tokens/min) may trigger the canary path, which we won’t charge extra for during the 3-month ramp.
- If LumenLabs needs guaranteed 95p latency under the absolute peak for every minute of the month, we’d need a reserved capacity addendum (higher commit / dedicated pool) — we can model that as an optional add-on in the SOW.

I’ll attach a DocuSign-ready SOW draft (SOW_v2) to this thread shortly.

— Ben
